passages.text:
LAC/ DAA Mileydi Guilarte's Participation in a Meeting with Meta
April 9, 2024, 1:30-2:30pm
Ronald Reagan Building (RRB) Meeting Room LAC Large Conference Room (5.09.040)
Google Meet
Context:
Meta's Director of Executive Branch Public Policy, Sandra Luff, reached out to you and
LAC AA Marcela Escobari to request a meeting given that Íñigo Fernández, Meta's Public Policy
Director for Meta in Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean will be in Washington, D.C. this
week. Meta requested a meeting "to provide an overview of our key workstreams, including an
update on Meta initiatives in the region, how we are addressing the root cause of migration,
and election integrity." (Tab 1) This meeting follows several engagements that LAC Bureau staff
have had with Meta, and with Mr. Fernandez in particular, over the last three years. Per GC
guidance, this meeting should not discuss specific Meta content or posts. If the conversation
veers toward discussions about having specific posts or content removed, retained, posted, or
promoted, USAID should redirect the conversation. USAID will mainly be in listening mode and
use additional talking points to follow-up on information shared or questions posted by Meta.
(Complete GC guidance in Tab 2)
Desired outcomes
• Listen to Meta's presentation of key workstreams, updates on initiatives in the region,
how they are addressing the root causes of migration, and election integrity.
• Express appreciation for Meta and Mr. Fernandez' engagement with USAID's LAC Bureau
and work with Central America Missions, including on election integrity, and under the
interagency Voices initiative and Central America Forward (CAF).
Participant List and Run-of-Show
The meeting will be held in the Ronald Reagan Building (RRB) and will be conducted in
English. As Meta requested the meeting, you will open the meeting, provide brief remarks, and
then give them the floor to hear their remarks. In line with GC guidance, you will mainly be in
listening mode, provide broad responses and turn to staff attending as needed, without
committing to concrete actions or next steps. Vera Zakem will join the meeting in-person at
1:50pm ET due to previous meeting commitments. She may provide some remarks when she
joins.
Participants
Meta
• Íñigo Fernández Baptista, Director of Public Policy for Mexico, Central America,
and the Caribbean
• Brian Townsend, Public Policy Manager for South America

relationships.title: Readout of Mileydi Guilarte’s meeting with Meta
relationships.evidence:
LAC/ DAA Mileydi Guilarte's Participation in a Meeting with Meta
April 9, 2024, 1:30-2:30pm
Ronald Reagan Building (RRB) Meeting Room LAC Large Conference Room (5.09.040)
Google Meet
Sandra Luff: Thank you. It's been a great partnership, and today our colleagues and I traveled
from Mexico. From our perspective, we would like to provide you with an update on our
priorities in the region and the partnerships that we not only have in DC but also with
embassies and civil societies. One of the things that we are talking about with the team is to
share what we are doing and to give you an opportunity to ask as many questions as possible.
Íñigo Fernández Baptista: Thank you for having us today. Also, I love coming here and learning
what your priorities are and how I can do my job better. I would like to focus on the results of
the several programs on which we are working. We have been working with the Partnership in
Central America, and we want to train them with digital skills. The second big area is developing
the southeastern states in Mexico
• We are focusing on indigenous communities, we are the first tech company to translate
their training to 7 indigenous languages, a lot of communities in Mexico are female
driven and we are focused on training female entrepreneurs. Another big point that we
need to step up is also creating digital citizenships. For a lot of the people who
experience the internet for the first time, what we are teaching them is that they have a
commitment to knowing what information they consume and what information they are
delivering.
• I want to thank you for your partnership. We have been able to provide training on
security best practices, and I think that's really made a difference.
Deborah Galindo: The USG is very focused on Honduras, Salvador, and Guatemala, and we are
expanding this initiative to Panama, DR and other central american countries. We are also
partnering with different organizations in Central America and focusing on women in business.
We are also partnering with different organizations to focus on women and entrepreneurs, and
our plan for 2024 is to partner with other members of the PCA, like MasterCard. We also want
to partner with other organizations that are not inside the PCA but are working closely with
them.
Mileydi Guilarte: Part of our limited footprint in Mexico is not only independent media but also
the disappearance. Is there anything else we can do or another opportunity to exclusively focus
on implementing partners?
Íñigo Fernández Baptista: It's tragic what is happening in Mexico. Being a journalist and human
rights advocate in Mexico is very dangerous. We do several things to empower them: we
